LESSON: ROCKS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY
Strand: Natural Systems and Processes
Topic 2.1: Rocks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rocks, part of Natural Systems and Processes in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY.

Key inquiry question: Why are there different types of rocks?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm the meaning of rocks and share in class, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views on the definition of rocks. Use print or digital resources to establish the classification of rocks (according to mode of formation and age), download images and display in class, Learners using print media could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm the meaning of rocks and share in class, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views on the definition of rocks. Use print or digital resources to establish the classification of rocks (according to mode of formation and age), download images and display in class, Learners using print media could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rocks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: The skill of making connections as the learner makes a collage showing the

distribution of rocks in Kenya and displays in class

● Learning to Learn: The skill of investigation as the learner carries out library research on the significance of rocks

in Kenya

● Citizenship: The skill of national and cultural identity as the learner draws sketch maps of Kenya showing the

distribution of rocks

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The skill of effective decision making is enhanced as learners carry out

field study, in groups, on rocks within the local environment and write a report.

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology is enhanced as learners use print or digital resources to

establish the classification of rocks (i.e. according to mode of formation and age), download images and display

in class.

Values:
● Patriotism: Learner shows citizenship as they draw sketch maps of Kenya showing the distribution of rocks

● Unity: Learner embraces each other as they carry out field study on rocks within the local environment

● Responsibility: Learners make a collage, in groups, showing the distribution of rocks in Kenya and display in

class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learner discusses the characteristics of rocks and make presentations in class

28

● Safety in class and school environment: Learner carries out field study on rocks within the local environment,

collects, classifies and display the samples in class

● First Aid: Learner carries out field study on rocks within the local environment.

● Critical Thinking: Learner carry out field study, in groups, on rocks within the local environment and write reports

Suggested Learning Resources:

Photographs and pictures, local and extended environment, maps, realia, manilla papers, gunny bags, cartons, digital

resources, charts, marker pens, sawdust, sand, approved textbooks and other printed resources, library resources,

museums, rock artefacts, whiteboards, marker pens, rock display case
